summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn requests a successor experiment for the Node API question b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-question-0, using previous_id b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-experiment and the revision reason that the basis changed: the post-removal proposal is now also issued with a non-expiring caller context from a goroutine and observed over a fixed 300 ms window, followed by stopping the node to identify the only escape, while the deadline-context member control is retained. The comparison set is: a proposal issued with a non-expiring context on a node that applied its own removal must return inside the observation window (expected violated), and the member control with a 200 ms deadline must return promptly without error (expected holds). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, the full sequence the experiment is built to capture - member control returns in 0 ms with no error; after the removal is applied the deadline-context call blocks for the whole timeout and reports only 'context deadline exceeded'; the background-context call does not return inside the 300 ms window at all; and it ends only once the node is stopped, returning 'raft: stopped'. This directly measures the case the previous interpretation recorded as unmeasured, so the formal receipt will be able to support a claim about a caller that supplies no deadline, and the prefix, scope and assumptions state the observation window, the goroutine-based witness and the stop intervention explicitly. The formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
